title: Arbitration and Conciliation Act s. 45 — Statutory provision (ACA s. 45)

content.overview: Section 45 requires a judicial authority seized of an action concerning a section 44 arbitration agreement to refer the parties to arbitration at the request of a party or person claiming through or under that party, unless the agreement is prima facie null and void, inoperative or incapable of being performed.

content.study:
Section 45 — Power of judicial authority to refer parties to arbitration

Section 45 requires a judicial authority seized of an action concerning a section 44 arbitration agreement to refer the parties to arbitration at the request of a party or person claiming through or under that party, unless the agreement is prima facie null and void, inoperative or incapable of being performed.

The Part II analysis must begin with the statutory definition and the Convention framework, then identify the exact condition or enforcement ground engaged. The statutory grounds should not be expanded by general merits review.
